title: A Decade of PhotoMappers: A Longitudinal Study of Crowdsourced Disaster Photos Geolocalization with Vision-Language Models and Geospatial Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2610.15403v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Crowdsourced disaster imagery provides timely, ground-level observations when conventional disaster mapping is delayed or incomplete, yet its geographic value depends on where observations are produced, how they are interpreted, and whether they can be reliably located as actionable Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT). Using more than a decade of PhotoMappers, a crowdsourced disaster-mapping initiative, this study examines the changing geography of disaster information and asks how emerging GeoAI models compare with human geographic interpretation. We combine longitudinal spatial analysis with cross-view geolocalization using street view imagery (SVI) and remote sensing imagery (RSI), and evaluate vision-language models (VLMs) reasoning through 30 indicators spanning geographic cues and reasoning evidence. translated_title: PhotoMappers的十年：基于视觉语言模型与地理空间推理的众包灾害照片地理定位纵向研究
translated_abstract: 众包灾害影像在传统灾害制图延迟或缺失时能够提供及时的地面观测，但其地理价值取决于观测产生的地点、如何被解读，以及能否被可靠地定位为可行动的地理空间情报（GEOINT）。本研究利用十多年来的PhotoMappers——一个众包灾害制图计划——考察了灾害信息的地理格局演变，并探究新兴的GeoAI模型与人类地理解读相比表现如何。我们将纵向空间分析与基于街景影像（SVI）和遥感影像（RSI）的跨视角地理定位相结合，并通过涵盖地理线索与推理证据的30项指标来评估视觉语言模型（VLM）的推理能力。结果揭示了一个在地理和时间上分布不均的灾害影像档案库，其形成受到不断变化的灾害类型、社区生命线（Community Lifelines）以及运行……
tldr: 本研究基于PhotoMappers十余年的众包灾害影像数据，结合纵向空间分析、街景与遥感影像的跨视角地理定位，以及30项指标对视觉语言模型推理能力的评估，系统揭示了灾害信息地理格局的时空演变，并比较了GeoAI与人类地理解读的差异。
en_tdlr: Leveraging over a decade of PhotoMappers crowdsourced disaster imagery, this study integrates longitudinal spatial analysis, cross-view geolocalization with street view and remote sensing imagery, and a 30-indicator evaluation of vision-language model reasoning to reveal the spatiotemporal evolution of disaster information geography and compare GeoAI with human geographic interpretation.
